newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BRAZILIAN ANDERSON KEEN ON BARCELONA MOVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZILIAN ANDERSON KEEN ON BARCELONA MOVE.

text.p: French champions Monaco's Brazilian striker Sonny Anderson, a leading candidate to fill the gap left by compatriot Ronaldo at Barcelona, said on Tuesday he was very keen on a move to the Spanish giants.
"A club like Barcelona interests me, that's for sure," Anderson said. "I'm aware of everything that's been said and written, the fees proposed, but I've not been contacted directly."
French media, including Tuesday's twice weekly France Football, have reported that Barcelona's new team boss Louis van Gaal has been interested in Anderson since his days as Ajax Amsterdam coach.

They have also said Barcelona would be prepared to pay about $22.5 million for the 26-year-old former Vasco da Gama, Guarani, Servette and Marseille striker, a sum many believe Monaco could not refuse.
Anderson, who is under contract with Monaco for five years, said he wanted a dialogue with his club's authorities because "my future is in play."
"It's very important for my future and my career," he said in a telephone interview, saying he would be disappointed if the move did not come off.

"If I have the chance of going to Barcelona there has to be a clear discussion because something exceptional is about to happen," said Anderson, who turned down the chance of a move to Paris St Germain a year ago.
"The possibility it seems I'm being offered of replacing Ronaldo is a very important challenge and I would like it to happen."
"It's also a chance for me to aspire to a place in the Brazilian national team and the World Cup," he added.

Monaco have refused to comment on whether they have been contacted by Barcelona over their striker, leading scorer in the French first division the 1995/96 season and third equal with 19 goals in their championship season.

During last month's Tournoi de France, Brazil coach Mario Zagallo said Anderson, who he has worked with at junior international level, was never out of the national team picture even though he has yet to win his first full cap.
